study type: Registry-based longitudinal study with interrupted time series analysis
cohort: The study included 1,762,422 births recorded in 12 Regional Birth Registries in Italy from January 2018 to December 2022.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic period was associated with a change in the pattern of preterm birth rates in Italy, lowering their average frequency by 5% from July 2020 onwards and interrupting a previous decreasing trend, with socio-economic maternal risk factors only marginally explaining this pattern.
